evals.name: bringup-and-health
evals.prompt: Get Intel's multimodal embedding service running locally with the CLIP/clip-vit-b-32 model and verify it is healthy.
evals.expected_output: Sets EMBEDDING_MODEL_NAME=CLIP/clip-vit-b-32, uses the prebuilt intel image (REGISTRY_URL=intel) with docker compose up -d, and verifies with GET http://localhost:9777/health.
expectations: Sets EMBEDDING_MODEL_NAME to CLIP/clip-vit-b-32 before starting the service
Starts the service from the prebuilt intel image via docker compose (no source build)
Verifies readiness with GET /health on port 9777

evals.name: text-embedding-request
evals.prompt: The embedding service is running on localhost:9777 with CLIP/clip-vit-b-32. Show me the exact request to embed the text 'a forklift in a warehouse'.
evals.expected_output: A POST /embeddings with JSON body {input: {type: 'text', text: '...'}, model: 'CLIP/clip-vit-b-32'}, returning an embedding vector.
expectations: Sends POST /embeddings with input shaped as {type: 'text', text: ...}
Includes a model field matching the loaded model (CLIP/clip-vit-b-32)

evals.name: video-url-embedding-request
evals.prompt: The embedding service is running on localhost:9777 with CLIP/clip-vit-b-32. Give me the request to embed the video at https://example.com/cam.mp4 sampling 16 frames, and tell me what the response looks like.
evals.expected_output: A POST /embeddings with input type video_url (video_url as a plain string) and segment_config {num_frames: 16}; the response contains one vector per sampled frame, not a single flat vector.
expectations: Uses input type video_url with video_url as a plain string field
States the response holds a list of per-frame vectors, not one flat vector

evals.name: model-capabilities-check
evals.prompt: Image requests to my embedding service return HTTP 400, but text requests work. It's running QwenText/qwen3-embedding-0.6b. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Nothing is broken: QwenText models are text-only, so image inputs are rejected by design. Points to GET /model/capabilities to check supported modalities and suggests a multimodal model (e.g. CLIP or SigLIP) if images are needed.
expectations: Explains QwenText models are text-only and the 400 is expected, not a service fault
References GET /model/capabilities to check supported modalities
Suggests a multimodal model family (e.g. CLIP or SigLIP) for image embedding

evals.name: negative-summarization-routing
evals.prompt: Use the multimodal embedding service to give me a text summary of this warehouse video.
evals.expected_output: Declines: the service returns embedding vectors, not text descriptions. Points to a vision-language model (e.g. OVMS-backed summarization pipeline) for summarization.
expectations: Does not claim the embedding service can produce a text summary
Explains embeddings are vectors for similarity/retrieval, not descriptions
Points to a VLM or summarization pipeline as the right tool
